command:
set -euo pipefail
cd /tmp

# The two inputs are the SAME ~400kb region assembled two ways -- spades (23 contigs)
# and megahit (2 contigs) from identical reads. Different assemblers give different
# contig layouts but the same underlying sequence, so their k-mer content is ~identical
# and mash distance is near zero. This cross-validates the assembly chain: garbage from
# either assembler would NOT be near-identical.
echo "== mash distance: spades assembly vs megahit assembly =="
mash dist spades_contigs.fa megahit_contigs.fa > mash-dist.txt
cat mash-dist.txt

DIST=$(awk 'NR==1{print $3}' mash-dist.txt)
SHARED=$(awk 'NR==1{print $5}' mash-dist.txt)
{
  echo "mash_distance   $DIST   want < 0.001   (same ~400kb region, two assemblers; observed 0.000168)"
  echo "shared_hashes   $SHARED   (observed 993/1000)"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt

# Method-justified threshold: two assemblies of identical sequence share nearly all
# k-mers, so mash (bottom-sketch MinHash) distance sits far below 0.001; a broken sketch
# or a mismatched pair gives distance >> 0.1. Not a value shaved to pass.
awk -v d="$DIST" 'BEGIN{ if (d+0 >= 0 && d+0 < 0.001) exit 0; print "mash distance " d " not < 0.001"; exit 1 }'
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
